summary: The code is syntactically valid and contains a reasonably detailed agent-based simulation scaffold with households, people, locations, a policy authority, media, and a supply chain. However, it does not fully implement the specified task: several required entities and metrics are missing or renamed, important validation criteria are absent, mandate end-day handling is unsafe (None handling), a validation function contains a critical runtime error ('mean' stray token), and multiple required outputs/behaviors (e.g., free mask distribution, policy cost) are not implemented.

issues.description: The implementation diverges from the required specification: missing or renamed entities (Retailer and Authority with free mask distribution), missing behaviors (free_mask_distribution, host_contacts), and multiple required metrics are not computed (e.g., average_adoption_rate, sustained_adoption_last_14_days, compliance_in_mandated_locations, subgroup_adoption_gap_income, masks_purchased_per_capita, policy_cost). Returned metric names also differ from the spec (e.g., adoption_rate instead of adoption_rate_over_time).
issues.solution: Add the specified entities and behaviors: implement Retailer with stock/price/restock and rationing, Authority with free_mask_distribution_rate and campaign/enforcement budget, and InformationChannel with reliability/misinformation_rate. Compute required metrics under the exact names: adoption_rate_over_time, average_adoption_rate, sustained_adoption_last_14_days, compliance_in_mandated_locations, subgroup_adoption_gap_income, masks_purchased_per_capita, policy_cost, stockout_days. Align return keys and internal tracking accordingly.

issues.description: validate_replicate_consistency ends with a stray 'mean' expression and never returns. This will raise a NameError if the function is called.
issues.solution: Remove the stray 'mean', compute coefficient of variation of 'finals' via statistics.pstdev/mean, compare to cv_threshold, and return (ok, msg). For example: cv = pstdev(finals)/(mean(finals)+1e-12); return cv <= cv_threshold, f"replicate_consistency: cv={cv:.3f}".

issues.description: Mandate end day handling assumes mandate_end_day is an int. The spec allows null (None). int(None) will raise a TypeError during initialization.
issues.solution: Allow mandate_end_day to be None. Store it as Optional[int] and in issue_mandates handle open-ended mandates: return self.mandate_enabled and day >= start and (self.mandate_end_day is None or day <= self.mandate_end_day).

issues.description: Required validation criteria are not implemented (adoption_bounds, convergence_last_14_days with per-day changes, mandate_effect_sanity_check, nonnegative_inventory, reproducibility_fixed_seed). Existing validation helpers differ in logic.
issues.solution: Implement the specified validation checks: (1) adoption_bounds: verify all adoption_rate_over_time in [0,1]; (2) convergence_last_14_days: count days among last 14 where abs(diff day-to-day) < 0.005 and require >=10; (3) mandate_effect_sanity_check: ensure adoption increases by >=5 percentage points within 14 days after mandate_start_day with enforcement_probability > 0; (4) nonnegative_inventory: verify all retailer/supply stock and agent inventories stay >=0; (5) reproducibility_fixed_seed: two runs with same seed produce identical time series.

issues.description: Policy cost and fines are not modeled. The spec requires policy_cost and fines collected; only enforcement_actions_count is returned.
issues.solution: Track fines assessed (= incident count * fine_amount when enforcement applies and mandate active), enforcement spending (e.g., per-check cost from enforcement_budget or per-incident cost), and campaign costs (campaign_intensity * cost per day). Compute policy_cost = enforcement + campaign - fines_collected. Return policy_cost and fines_collected metrics.

issues.description: No implementation of free mask distribution, which is required by the spec (free_mask_distribution_rate).
issues.solution: Add a daily loop where the authority distributes min(rate, available stock) masks to eligible persons (e.g., randomly among low-income or those with zero inventory), incrementing their mask_inventory accordingly, and decrementing supply or a separate distribution stock.

issues.description: Reproducibility validation not implemented to guarantee identical outputs for same seed; a counterfactual run inside Simulation.run changes state but uses a different seed and is unnecessary.
issues.solution: Move counterfactual analysis outside core run or make it optional. Implement a dedicated reproducibility test that runs Simulation twice with the same params and seed and checks series equality. Avoid side-effect-prone global state.

issues.description: Income subgroup adoption gap metric (top vs bottom quintile) is missing; a Gini across quintiles is provided but not the requested gap.
issues.solution: Compute subgroup_adoption_gap_income: adoption rate in top income quintile minus bottom income quintile and include it in results under the exact name.

issues.description: The simulation replaces the Retailer with a SupplyChain. The spec mandates purchase_and_supply with Retailer stock, price, daily_restock, rationing. This affects stockout_days and masks_purchased_per_capita.
issues.location: SupplyChain class and purchase flow in Simulation.step
issues.solution: Introduce one or more Retailer entities with stock, price, restock, rationing_policy, and region. Route purchases through retailers, track per-retailer stockouts to compute stockout_days, and track masks_purchased_per_capita.

issues.description: compliance_in_mandated_locations metric is not explicitly computed; only overall compliance and under_mandate averages are reported.
issues.solution: When mandate_active, compute fraction wearing masks among those present in mandated locations (public/work that are policy_eligible) and record as compliance_in_mandated_locations. Aggregate over time as needed.

issues.description: Parameter validation is minimal. Several parameters expected in [0,1] are not validated, and unsafe casts (e.g., int(None)) may occur.
issues.solution: Add defensive normalization and checks (clamp or defaults) for probabilities, handle None values safely, and raise informative errors or coerce to defaults where appropriate.

issues.description: With population_size=10000, iterating over all persons and all public locations daily and sampling contacts per person may be slow in pure Python.
issues.solution: Consider reducing default population or venues for typical runs, vectorizing some computations (e.g., use numpy), caching neighbor samples, or sub-sampling visits for performance. Provide parameters to downscale simulation for validation/CI.

issues.description: Unused imports (argparse, json, DATA_DIR constants) and environment path setup are present but unused.
issues.solution: Remove unused imports and constants or implement CLI/IO that uses them.

issues.description: Main function is empty; while the system requires a direct main() call, having it do nothing impairs usability.
issues.solution: Optionally add a simple demo runner or CLI parsing to run the simulation with default params and print/save results. Keep the direct main() call to satisfy the system requirement.
